entries.userVisibleSummary: Keiko 0.3.0 completes the release-readiness program: multi-root editor workspaces with an explicit Workspace Trust gate, editor profiles and per-file local history, approximate-nearest-neighbour local knowledge retrieval, and a governed Coding Workbench whose runtime actions are bound to the authenticated launcher session. Every autonomy-capable surface now reports readiness truthfully instead of showing green over an unusable gateway, and failed actions surface a diagnosable error instead of failing silently.

stateImpact.description: The local UI store migrates forward automatically on first start (schema 9 to 19). Migrations are additive: new tables for workspace manifests, workspace trust, editor profiles, local history, coding-runtime snapshots and memory autonomy policy, plus new columns on existing chat rows. No existing row is deleted or rewritten destructively. After the migration an older Keiko binary refuses to open the store rather than corrupting it.

Workspaces become explicit manifests with per-root trust decisions. An existing single-folder binding is migrated into a one-root manifest. The first time a workspace is opened, Keiko starts in Restricted Mode and asks for an explicit trust decision before scripts, language servers or agent execution are available.

Local knowledge retrieval moves to an approximate-nearest-neighbour index built on demand from the vectors already stored. Stored encrypted vectors remain intact and are reused, so no pod has to be re-indexed; only cached materialization state is discarded and rebuilt.

Coding Workbench state-changing actions are bound to the authenticated, launcher-attested browser session. A window that is not paired with the launcher can read status but is refused run start, approvals, stop/takeover and follow-up prompts, and the surface now says so instead of appearing ready.

releaseNoteBullets: Added multi-root editor workspaces with an explicit Workspace Trust gate: a new workspace opens in Restricted Mode until you grant trust, and scripts, language servers and agent execution stay unavailable until you do.
Added editor profiles, portable profile import and export, and per-file local history with a keyboard-operable timeline and honest restore.
Local knowledge now uses an approximate-nearest-neighbour index for retrieval, built on demand from the vectors already stored; existing pods do not need to be re-indexed.

Coding Workbench, Chat, Git, Prompt Enhancer, MemoriaViva and Quality Intelligence now report readiness and outcomes truthfully: no green state over an unusable gateway, no silent failure, and every refused action names its reason with a copyable support id.
Voice turns now carry their staged attachments and document context, and interrupting the assistant cancels only the answer it owns instead of blocking sending elsewhere.
Governed Git delivery authenticates on every network path, reports commit signing honestly, and distinguishes offline from authentication failures instead of reporting one generic error.

review.rationale: The maintainer explicitly commissioned the 0.3.0 release in the local session and directed the portable delivery scope (bundled Node.js and OpenCode sidecar for macOS and Windows). The entry covers the release-readiness audit programme tracked in epic #2802 and the implementation waves merged into dev. The approval evidence is the release owner's authored comment on the epic issue #2802 (comment 5225214175), carrying the version-bound phrase 'Approved-for-publish: @oscharko-dev/keiko@0.3.0' on a line of its own; the publish gate verifies the comment, its issue binding, the phrase, and the allow-listed author through the GitHub API (GitHub refuses self-approval of one's own pull request, so the solo owner cannot mint a PR-review artifact).

entries.userVisibleSummary: Keiko 0.3.1 is the first public download release. It carries the same product as 0.3.0 and republishes it under a usable tag: the 0.3.0 GitHub release was withdrawn during verification and GitHub keeps that tag immutable, so the downloadable packages ship as 0.3.1. Nothing has to be uninstalled or migrated. An older build left running only occupies the local port, and the new one says so on startup and names both ways out (stop it, or start on another port). The governed one-click update does not apply to this release: its portable evidence declares the evaluation signing status, and the updater accepts only production-signed, notarized portable artifacts. Install it from the GitHub Release download; the in-app update returns once the signed lane ships.

stateImpact.description: No schema change relative to 0.3.0. A store created by 0.3.0 opens unchanged; a store from 0.2.x migrates forward exactly as 0.3.0 described.

releaseNoteBullets: First public download release: unsigned evaluation bundles for macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel) and Windows, with Node.js and the OpenCode sidecar included. macOS needs one right-click - Open on first launch; Windows shows the SmartScreen notice.
Load an existing keiko.config.json directly in the setup dialog instead of typing every field.
Upgrading from 0.3.0 needs no migration. If an older Keiko is still running it holds the local port; stop it or start this one with --port.

review.rationale: Republication of the 0.3.0 product under a usable release tag, directed by the release owner after the 0.3.0 GitHub release was withdrawn during verification and its tag became immutable. This single record also carries the portable runtime staging contract, unchanged from 0.3.0 (program epic and the same three targets, staging only): 0.3.1 is one release event with one owner approval, so splitting it across two records would need a second approval artifact for the same decision. The evidence is the release owner's authored comment on epic #2802 (comment 5230996334) carrying the version-bound publish phrase on a line of its own, verified live by the publish gate.

entries.userVisibleSummary: Keiko 0.3.2 carries the same product as 0.3.1 and completes its publication: the npm latest dist-tag points at the current release again, so a plain npm install delivers today's Keiko instead of a 0.2.x build. The release pipeline that blocked the 0.3.1 npm promotion was repaired end to end - the publisher verifies the four published downloads (three archives and the Windows setup companion) byte for byte against build-run artifacts fetched by their immutable ids (a rerun can neither substitute bytes nor block a verified release), no longer refuses over per-target evidence files, resolves its own operating conditions (release-owner allowlist, transport policy, provenance attestation only where an OIDC provider exists), and states every unmet precondition before the gate chain runs. The project README was rewritten around the product. Nothing has to be uninstalled or migrated; the governed one-click update still does not apply while the portable line ships with evaluation signing.

stateImpact.description: No schema change relative to 0.3.1. A store created by 0.3.0 or 0.3.1 opens unchanged; a store from 0.2.x migrates forward exactly as 0.3.0 described.

releaseNoteBullets: npm installs follow the current release again: the latest dist-tag points at 0.3.2, so a plain npm install delivers today's Keiko.

The release pipeline verifies the four portable downloads byte for byte against build-run artifacts fetched by immutable id; a workflow rerun can neither substitute release bytes nor block a verified release.
The project README now leads with the product: what Keiko does, the downloads, and a two-command quickstart.

review.rationale: Completion of the 0.3.1 release event: the npm latest promotion was blocked by a defect in the publish verification itself, repaired in #3055, and the repaired pipeline requires a version whose tag can still carry a release. 0.3.2 ships the identical product with the repaired release machinery and the product-first README; the evidence is the release owner's authored comment on epic #2802 carrying the version-bound publish phrase on a line of its own, verified live by the publish gate.
